title: November 8: BrainRailRoad turns phase yards into an auditable learning experiment
summary: One new repository extends the November 8 turntable family into a hard-event differentiable training laboratory. Python/JavaScript parity and supervised gradients work; initial railway learning fails through silence while a 15-unit GRU learns the same task under a documented five-seed development control. Earlier 15-commit activity counts are historical and are not reattributed to this addition.

nodes.claim: Phase-addressed, hard-event 12-hidden-yard/2-output railway with 36 active of 90 candidate directed rails, four phase release addresses, 32-tick exit clocks, simulated apical/basket/chandelier controls and supervised surrogate-BPTT search for contextual A/B order classification.
nodes.survived: Python/JavaScript hard-event parity and real offline browser execution are implemented. Source reports nonzero finite parameter gradients and separate five-seed 15-hidden-unit GRU controls: median 100% frozen interpolation, 99.61% ±2-tick jitter and 95.12% out-of-range gaps. Later one-seed hard-reference rescue: optional first-stimulus pilot reset removes full output silence under randomized onset, but yields a one-sided event code. Fixed-onset original and randomized-onset reset both preserve order information as fire-versus-silence.
nodes.killed: The railway has NOT learned the classification task in reported development runs: output silence/ties cause abstention. Working gradients and a successful GRU baseline establish trainability of the task and operational plumbing, not trained railway performance, autonomous local plasticity, energy advantage or biological realism. A four-configuration CPU rescue and 600-update extension never exceeded 50% hard validation accuracy; one order has zero H2/output events. At empty yards, upstream weight/delay/topology credit vanishes through zero vector magnitude; removing the empty-yard mask alone changes only spurious threshold gradients.
nodes.era: November 8: phase trains and growing rails

edges.why: BrainRailRoad explicitly cites the earlier phase-selective turntable, phase-addressed release and receiver timing as prior work, reimplemented in a larger hard-event model; this is conceptual lineage, not proof of shared source files.

The nine-yard apical/basket/chandelier computational roles motivate corresponding interventions in the 12-hidden-yard trainable hard-event system; separate implementation, not demonstrated file ancestry.

Both explore modifiable railway structure and delayed delivery, but BrainRailRoad uses globally supervised surrogate topology selection whereas KasvavatKiskotSol uses destination-ACK structural material reinforcement.
Both treat timing as operational and candidate rail structure as variable; the ant-like path-memory growth and the supervised hard-event classifier remain algorithmically distinct.

motifs.title: A runnable phase-addressed circuit is not yet a learned phase-addressed circuit
motifs.description: Hard forward events, browser parity, nonzero surrogate gradients, frozen splits and a strong GRU comparator distinguish simulator correctness, task learnability and the still-unsolved railway training objective. The topology/weights/delays are trained nonlocally, unlike locally grown material rails. A measured stimulus-reset rescue makes timing readable but does not turn one-sided fire-versus-silence discrimination into two correct labeled outputs; zero-vector gradients prevent silent-path credit.
